description:
Create many DNS records on a Porkbun domain in one call — the companion to scan_dns_records for keeping a transferred domain working. Pass `records` to import an exact list (preferred when you read the zone from the old registrar's API), or omit it entirely to import whatever a live scan of the domain discovers. Idempotent: a record that already exists is reported in `skipped`, not `failed`, so this is safe to re-run and safe as a converge step. Individual failures are listed in `failures` while everything else still imports. NS and SOA entries are ignored on purpose — they describe the delegation, not the zone. Important: imported records have no effect until the domain actually points at Porkbun's nameservers, so check get_nameservers afterwards and use update_nameservers when the user is ready to cut over — when the domain is delegated elsewhere the response also says so in `warnings`. Maximum 500 records per call.

On this server the records may come from a file (records_file, JSON, or zone_file, a BIND zone file) instead of inline, and every record's content is checked before any is sent: a DKIM key must parse, an SPF record must have no obvious mistake. One that fails refuses the whole import, naming the record.

domain.description: Porkbun domain to create the records on, e.g. `example.com`

records.description: Exact records to create. Omit to import what a live scan of the domain finds.

name.description: Subdomain prefix only, or empty string for the apex. `@` and a fully-qualified name are both accepted.

ttl.description: Seconds. Raised to the API minimum if lower.

records_file.description: Instead of records: a JSON file holding the array (or an object with it under `records`), read byte-exact by this server, so a long list is not retyped. The answer adds records_file: its sha256, size and how many records it held. Never type or paste a file's base64 yourself: a retyped file can arrive changed. Give the path of a file in your workspace folders (the roots this client shares; without them /tmp/churn-nhb_syf1), or have a script that read the file send content_base64 with its sha256.

content_base64.description: The file's bytes as standard base64, only as a script that read the file wrote them, never typed. Needs sha256.

path.description: The records file: a file in your workspace folders (the roots this client shares with the server; without them /tmp/churn-nhb_syf1); a bare name is taken from the first. Links are refused. Exactly one of path or content_base64.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the file, as sha256sum prints it. Required with content_base64, checked with path.

zone_file.description: Instead of records: a BIND zone file (RFC 1035: $ORIGIN, $TTL, @, relative names, parentheses, quoted TXT), such as export_dns_zone writes or another DNS host exports, read byte-exact by this server. Its names must be in the domain. SOA, NS and DNSSEC records are not imported and are listed in the answer's zone_file.ignored; a type Porkbun cannot hold, $INCLUDE or a line that does not parse refuses the whole import, naming the line. The answer adds zone_file: its sha256, size, how many records it held and what was ignored. Never type or paste a file's base64 yourself: a retyped file can arrive changed. Give the path of a file in your workspace folders (the roots this client shares; without them /tmp/churn-nhb_syf1), or have a script that read the file send content_base64 with its sha256.

content_base64.description: The file's bytes as standard base64, only as a script that read the file wrote them, never typed. Needs sha256.

path.description: The zone file: a file in your workspace folders (the roots this client shares with the server; without them /tmp/churn-nhb_syf1); a bare name is taken from the first. Links are refused. Exactly one of path or content_base64.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the file, as sha256sum prints it. Required with content_base64, checked with path.

name: import_dns_records
